sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Wyandot County, Ohio?
sections.html:
You record it with the Wyandot County Recorder in Room 24 of the courthouse at 109 South Sandusky Avenue, Upper Sandusky, OH 43351. The office phone is 419-294-1442, and the same address serves as the mailing address. Two deputy recorders work under the elected Recorder.

Wyandot is a rural county. The legislature organized it on February 3, 1845 from pieces of Crawford, Marion, Hardin and Hancock counties, and it covers 408 square miles in the northwest part of the state. Upper Sandusky is the only city and the county seat. The 2020 census counted 21,900 people in 9,084 households, with 9,839 housing units, 7.7 percent of them vacant. About 73.5 percent of occupied homes are owner occupied, and nearly 70 percent of residents live in rural areas.

That rural makeup shapes deeds here. Many Wyandot parcels are farm tracts or township acreage described by section, township and range, so the legal description gets more scrutiny than it would for a platted city lot.

sections.h2: Why does a Wyandot County deed stop at the Tax Map Department first?
sections.html:
The county's written conveyance standards say no deed will be accepted for transfer by the Auditor or for recording by the Recorder until the Engineer's Tax Map Department has reviewed and stamped it. The stamp reads Description Checked, Tax Map Office. The department has moved into the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street.

The reviewer takes one of four paths on an ordinary sale with an unchanged description:

  • Approve the description as written and stamp the deed.
  • Suggest fixes for obvious typing errors, transposed numbers or rotated bearings, then stamp it.
  • Let a description with a clear point of beginning but minor flaws transfer one time, with a notice that a survey is required on the next non-exempt transfer.
  • Stamp a bad description Survey Required.

The standards define a bad description as one whose point of beginning cannot be identified or that contains an error causing ambiguity. Examples they list include missing dimensions or acreage, no section, township and range or municipality, and a parcel the grantor does not own. The county encourages authors to have descriptions checked before the closing date so a correction does not delay the sale.

sections.h2: Which Wyandot County transfers can skip a new survey?
sections.html:
Exempt transfers with no money changing hands can move with an older description that fails today's standards, and the deed gets the same survey-required notice. The standards list inheritance by survivorship, transfers into or out of a family trust, transfers to an immediate family member, life estates, corrective deeds, court ordered transfers, and sheriff's and auditor's deeds.

A sale for money does not qualify. If your house sits on an acreage tract and the deed description is vague, expect the reviewer to ask for a survey before the next buyer's deed can go through. New splits of an existing parcel need a survey recorded in the county survey records, a closure report, and at least three working days for inspection. New parcels need 40 feet of owned highway frontage for single family housing and 60 feet for multiple family housing. Parcels that miss the 200 foot road frontage rule in the regional planning checklist must meet those minimums. Call Wyandot County Regional Planning at 419-294-4931 before you plan a split.

sections.h2: What do the Ohio statutes require of the deed itself?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5301.01 says the grantor signs the deed and acknowledges the signing before a judge or court clerk, county auditor, county engineer, notary public or mayor. Ohio Revised Code 317.13 directs the Recorder to record instruments in the order presented and to note the date and exact time of presentation, which fixes priority between competing filings.

The same section allows the Recorder to refuse an instrument that the Revised Code does not authorize for recording or that appears materially false or fraudulent. A person who is refused can ask the Common Pleas Court to order the recording. The statute also required every recorder to offer electronic recording of conveyances and online indexes back to January 1, 1980 by June 30, 2026, so ask the Wyandot office which electronic options it uses.

sections.h2: Which transfers owe the Auditor's conveyance fee?
sections.html:
Most sales do, and the grantor pays it. Ohio Revised Code 319.54 sets the fee at one dollar, or ten cents for each one hundred dollars or fraction of one hundred dollars of value, whichever is greater. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 requires a statement of value before the Auditor endorses the deed. For a sale, value means the full price paid or to be paid, including any mortgage or lien on the property.

Transfers the statute excludes from the Auditor's conveyance fee
Type of transferFee under 319.54(G)(3)
Gift between spouses, or parent and childNot charged
Among heirs or devisees of one decedent, no money paidNot charged
Into a trust the grantor can revokeNot charged
To confirm or correct a recorded deedNot charged
Sale to a buyer for moneyCharged at the rate above

Source: Ohio Revised Code 319.54. The statute lists more exemptions, such as court ordered transfers that are not sales.

A county may also levy a real property transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars under Ohio Revised Code 322.02, paid by the grantor to the Auditor before recording. Ask the Wyandot County Auditor whether one applies.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Wyandot County Recorder?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 317.32 sets $17 plus a $17 housing trust fund fee for the first two pages and $4 plus $4 for each additional page. A preservation surcharge of up to $5 may be added. Call the Recorder at 419-294-1442 for the total on your document, because a long metes and bounds description adds pages.

Sellers can lower the odds of a rejected filing by pulling the previous deed first. The conveyance standards require a new metes and bounds description to cite the prior deed and the recorded source of any exception, and to state acreage to the third decimal place when a new description is written. If a tract is conveyed with exceptions, the standards allow no more than four.

sections.h2: How do I research a Wyandot County parcel before listing it?
sections.html:
The Tax Map Department helps the public locate property, verify ownership, and assign new addresses in unincorporated areas. Its county page offers downloads of tax maps, property surveys and legal descriptions, plus a current parcel data file in ZIP format that the county supplies as is, with no guarantee of accuracy. The County Auditor keeps an online tax map site as well.

The county says plainly that this is a tax map system and not a full GIS, and Wyandot has no GIS department for advanced requests. A seller with an older farm or edge of town house can gather three things before talking to a buyer:

  • The parcel number and acreage the Auditor shows on the tax map.
  • The last recorded deed, with its legal description and any exceptions.
  • Any recorded survey for the tract, which settles whether a survey will be demanded on the next transfer.

Comparing the deed acreage with the tax map matters because the standards for older descriptions that are not metes and bounds tolerate a difference of only 0.2 acre on parcels under 5 acres and 5 percent on larger ones.

faqs.q: Do I need a survey to sell a house in Wyandot County?
faqs.a: Not always. A sale with an unchanged description can transfer after the Tax Map Department stamps it. A bad description gets a Survey Required stamp, and splits of a parcel always need a recorded survey.

faqs.q: Where is the Wyandot County Tax Map Department?
faqs.a: It operates from the County Engineer's office at 320 N. Warpole Street in Upper Sandusky, after moving from its earlier location.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Wyandot County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor, which is the seller. The fee is the greater of one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars of value under Ohio Revised Code 319.54.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Wyandot County Recorder?
faqs.a: Call 419-294-1442. The office is in Room 24 at 109 South Sandusky Avenue in Upper Sandusky.

faqs.q: Can the Recorder reject my deed?
faqs.a: Yes, if the instrument is not authorized for recording or looks materially false or fraudulent. Revised Code 317.13 lets the filer ask the Common Pleas Court to order the Recorder to record it.
